checks.check: Migration backfills existing employee-ID accounts without guessing legacy identities
Migration is re-runnable without duplicate records/history and publishes the private attendance revision table
Registration preflight accepts new numbers and cannot create or expose employee records
One signup atomically creates the employee, pending User profile and linked access request
An existing employee number reuses the exact HR row and preserves names, email and monitoring histories
The database also rejects duplicate employee numbers introduced by manual Admin encoding
Duplicate requests are blocked while distinct leading-zero employee numbers remain distinct
An Admin employee update signals only the linked account for attendance refresh
Approved users receive only their own attendance/uniform records and cannot open the personnel directory
Attendance signals are read-only and caller-owned; personnel and visitor notifications stay Admin-only
URL-style ID arguments, profile edits and forged Auth metadata cannot redirect attendance
Admin can link an older User account by employee number while retaining exclusive personnel-directory access
Administrator HR corrections keep the permanent attendance link and employee-number login resolver
Trusted administrator setup remains supported; administrator-created Users also receive linked employees
A failed request rolls back Auth, profile and employee creation without orphan records
